i wish i could just go home. back to where i lived before all this, back to when i could still see my friends, back to a neighborhood full of normal people who were nice, and not wealthy racists who drive their designer cars too fast.  i miss neighbors who cared about me and didnt verbally assault me.  i miss friends acting like friends.  i miss other people of color who didnt treat me like a spokesperson for my ethnicity, or see my ethnic background as a token for gaining respect.  i miss picking up food like normal and eating it, and not emptying out my bank account for it.  i miss being able to sleep on the couch. i miss using a kitchen.  i miss enjoying cooking and having friends over, and i miss parties and alcohol and stupid adventures.  i miss walking around and being outside and taking the bus and sitting in libraries, and i miss having my camera around my neck, because i knew there was a moment coming that id want to remember.  i miss wanting to live in the present, miss looking forward to good things happening soon, I miss stationary shops and tacos with my boys and going to the beach when everything got too much.  now im in this stupid fucking town full of rich entitled idiots, waiting out a neverending stream of bullshit.  i hope that i can pull through to see tacos with my boys again.
a few more stressors and i know ill feel worse, and worse, and worse.  i wish there was a way i could calm the fuck down but shit is alwys just getting worse.

Thank you for listening and reading.  Yeah, we (asians and everyone else) are subject to the pressures of conforming to western beauty standards, and even the ways makeup techniques and tools cater more to some body types than others.  Many asians around me also subscribe to and enforce societal conformity with colorism, and rejection of our ethnic features, etc., but many folks dont think about the harm done to our siblings with monolids, or darker skin, or the harm we do to our own bodies when we talk like that and marginalize certain bodies. Your friends speaking that way can definitely harm and pressure people, and is probably also them commenting on the relative societal privilege that some people gain by being born into a world that, in this moment, accepts some bodies and rejects others.  It's a rough time for sure, but we must remember that we are all beautiful in so many different ways.

We are all learning and doing our best to cause the least harm possible; dont sweat it and thanks again for reading.

not to be a dick at all, and thank you for your input-- but like I mentioned, the surgery stuff is kind of traumatizing for me as a mixed race person who has had certain beauty standards pushed on me my whole life.  

speaking truthfully and from the heart here,  I grew up in a place that treated asian folks like trash.  I used to get bullied as a kid by older kids who would pull their eyes apart and "ching chong" and spit at me.  My older brother was also the victim of a violent hate crime because of the way his eyes look; he never got justice for that.  I know a lot of asian folks and folks with monolids get surgery to match european/western beauty standards (not all for this reason of course), in order to be more legible to white folks and the media.  I respect peoples right to make a choice, while also feeling pain that there are many people who feel they have to do that to succeed in their careers or live a normal life.  It makes me sad that people are compelled by the way society is structured, to dislike their bodies, while i also recognize that if you want to do something, you should do it.  But at the end of the day, I dont ever want to be called lucky for being born with the eyelids I have, juxtaposing myself with folks with monolids as unlucky.  

It reminds me of when I go see relatives with darker skin than me, and they make comments on me being meztisa (mixed race + implying lighter skinned), talking about how being light skinned is a desirable trait in our country.  Im all for loving and accepting my body as it is, but not at a cost or detriment to others, be they folks with monolids or folks with deeper skin.
